observation.visible_scene: A sunlit garden border seen in strong backlight: a large dark reddish-purple tree fills the left background, a bright yellow-green tree the right, a rounded clipped hedge sits mid-right, and a foreground row of reddish-brown leafy shrubs mixed with pale green plants stands above a strip of grass. A prominent green circular lens flare hovers in the upper-left, and a second green flare orb appears lower-right in later frames.
visible_changes: The whole scene translates horizontally to the right across the frame over the clip, while new content (a magenta/purple flower bed) enters from the left edge and the rounded hedge and yellow tree drift toward and partly off the right edge — a coherent shift of all depth layers together, indicating a steady camera pan (looking progressively leftward) rather than object motion.
The upper-left green lens flare moves rightward and slightly downward in sync with the pan; a brighter green flare orb grows into view at the lower-right as the camera rotates.

Foreground shrub and hedge positions relative to the frame change only by this shared translation; no individual plant is seen to grow, fall, or be struck, and any leaf-level sway is too subtle to confirm.
The clip ends mid-pan with the hedge still near the right edge and the purple bed still at the left, so the motion is ongoing rather than completed.
outside_clip_unknowns: What lies further left (beyond the purple bed) and further right (beyond the hedge/yellow tree) before and after this segment.
Whether the pan was already in progress before frame 1 and whether it continues past frame 41.
The cause of the backlighting and flare (sun position, lens orientation) is not visible.
Any wind or leaf motion independent of the camera is not established.
uncertain_details: Exact pan type (rotational pan vs lateral tracking) cannot be separated from these frames alone.
Slight apparent jitter/size change of individual leaves may be compression or minor sway, not confirmed object motion.
The lower-right green orb is most consistent with a lens flare artifact tied to the moving sun, not a separate physical object.
